charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Segment Revenue: Commodities vs Life Sciences
charts.annotation: Only available from FY2025 onward -- ALS restructured from three reporting segments (Commodities, Life Sciences, Industrial) to two, so earlier periods are not comparable and are left blank rather than estimated.

charts.title: Statutory vs Underlying NPAT & EBIT
charts.annotation: Underlying figures are ALS's own non-IFRS measures (significant items -- restructuring, impairments, acquisition costs -- added back); statutory figures are as reported under IFRS. Both series are only available from FY2025 onward.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For ALS Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For ALS Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For ALS Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For ALS Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For ALS Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For ALS Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For ALS Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For ALS Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For ALS Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For ALS Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

segmentMix.title: Segment revenue mix
segmentMix.content:
ALS reports through two segments: Commodities (mining, mineral, energy and industrial testing) and Life Sciences (environmental, food, pharmaceutical/clinical and consumer products testing).

For ALS Limited: Commodities is ~39% of FY2026 revenue and the more cyclical leg, geared to mineral exploration and critical-minerals demand (FY2027 guidance: 13-15% organic growth, versus mid-single-digit for Life Sciences); Life Sciences at ~61% is the steadier, less commodity-price-sensitive base. ALS restructured out of a prior three-segment model (which also separately reported Industrial) in FY2025, so the split is only shown from FY2025 onward -- earlier periods are not comparable and are deliberately left blank.

What to watch:

  • Commodities growth decelerating if mineral exploration activity cools
  • Life Sciences margin drag from softer, pricing-pressured Environmental testing

statutoryVsUnderlying.title: Statutory vs underlying earnings
statutoryVsUnderlying.content:
ALS reports underlying NPAT and EBIT alongside statutory (IFRS) figures, adding back "significant items" -- restructuring costs, impairments, acquisition/integration costs and similar one-offs -- to show what management considers the run-rate result.

For ALS Limited: management guides the market on underlying measures (FY2026: underlying NPAT +25.8% to A$381.2m, underlying EBIT +19.3% to A$599.0m) and the gap to statutory net income/operating income is the size of the add-backs in a given year. Only shown from FY2025 onward, matching the periods captured in the kpis table.

What to watch:

  • Significant items recurring every year rather than being genuinely one-off
  • The statutory-underlying gap widening after an acquisition
